exact_text:
(1) This Act may be called the Code on Wages, 2019.
(2) It extends to the whole of India.
(3) It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint; and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Code and any reference in any such provision to the commencement of this Code shall be construed as a reference to the coming into force of that provision.
legal_status_notes: Brought into force w.e.f. 21 November 2025 vide Gazette Notification S.O. 5322(E).
In force w.e.f. 21 November 2025. 50% cap on excluded allowances.

section_or_rule_title: Fixation of minimum rate of wages
exact_text:
(1) Subject to the provisions of section 9, the appropriate Government shall fix the minimum rates of wages payable to employees in accordance with the provisions of section 8.
(2) For the purpose of sub-section (1), the appropriate Government may fix a minimum rate of wages for time work or piece work.
(6) In fixing minimum rates of wages under this section, the appropriate Government shall take into account the skill of workers (unskilled, skilled, semi-skilled, highly-skilled) and geographical area.

section_or_rule_title: Fixing hours of work for normal working day

exact_text: Where an employee whose minimum rate of wages has been fixed under this Code works on any day in excess of the number of hours constituting a normal working day, the employer shall pay him for every hour or for part of an hour so worked in excess, at the overtime rate which shall not be less than twice the normal rate of wages.
legal_status_notes: In force w.e.f. 21 November 2025. Overtime at not less than twice normal wages.
key_topics: work in excess of normal hours

exact_text: All wages shall be paid in current coin or currency notes or by cheque or by crediting the wages in the bank account of the employee or by the electronic mode.
legal_status_notes: In force w.e.f. 21 November 2025. Authorizes bank transfer, electronic mode, cheque, or currency notes.

exact_text: The employer shall fix the wage period for employees either as daily, weekly, fortnightly or monthly, and no wage period shall exceed one month.
legal_status_notes: In force w.e.f. 21 November 2025. Prohibits wage periods exceeding one month.

section_or_rule_title: Time limit for payment of wages and final settlement after resignation or termination
legal_status_notes: CRITICAL IN-FORCE SETTLEMENT RULE: In force w.e.f. 21 November 2025. Section 17(2) explicitly mandates payment of all wages within TWO WORKING DAYS of resignation, removal, dismissal, retrenchment, or closure.

section_or_rule_title: Deductions which may be made from wages
legal_status_notes: In force w.e.f. 21 November 2025. Exhaustively lists lawful deductions and caps total deductions at 50% of wages.

exact_text:
(1) The appropriate Government may, by notification, appoint one or more authorities, not below the rank of a Gazetted Officer, to hear and determine the claims which arises under the provisions of this Code.
(2) The authority appointed under sub-section (1), while deciding the claim under that sub-section, may order, having regard to the circumstances under which the claim arises, the payment of compensatory amount in addition to the claim amount which may extend to ten times of the claim amount and the employer shall be liable to pay such amount.
(3) An application under sub-section (1) may be filed by the employee concerned, or any Trade Union registered under the Trade Unions Act, 1926... or the Inspector-cum-Facilitator.
(6) An application under sub-section (1) shall be presented within a period of three years from the date on which the claim arose: Provided that the authority may admit an application after the expiry of the said period of three years, if the applicant satisfies the authority that he had sufficient cause for not making the application within such period.
legal_status_notes: In force w.e.f. 21 November 2025. 3 years limitation for filing wage claims; up to ten times compensation for delayed/unpaid wages.

exact_text:
(1) The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, the Minimum Wages Act, 1948, the Payment of Bonus Act, 1965 and the Equal Remuneration Act, 1976 are hereby repealed.
(2) Notwithstanding such repeal, anything done or any action taken or purported to have been done or taken under the enactments hereby repealed shall, in so far as it is not inconsistent with the provisions of this Code, be deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of this Code.
(3) The mention of particular matters in sub-section (2) shall not be held to prejudice or affect the general application of section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 with regard to the effect of repeal.
legal_status_notes: Operative w.e.f. 21 November 2025. Expressly repealed Payment of Wages Act 1936 and Minimum Wages Act 1948 subject to Section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 savings for pre-21-Nov-2025 rights and liabilities.
